title: About 20 Bangladeshi workers stranded in Laos without jobs or passports
excerpt: They went with government clearance for restaurant jobs that did not exist. A survivors' group has asked the expatriates' welfare ministry for food, shelter and repatriation.

image.alt: Pha That Luang in Vientiane, Laos
image.credit: File photo: Benh LIEU SONG / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0

content:
About 20 Bangladeshi workers who went to Laos with clearance from the Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET) for promised restaurant jobs have found neither the jobs nor the employer, The Daily Star reported on Tuesday (24 November).

One worker, Rifat Hasan Rabbi from Kishoreganj, told the paper that a local agency took their passports at the airport. He said the workers are living in five rooms near Vientiane, rely on money from families to eat, and had been told by their landlord to leave. He said the agency was demanding Tk 1 lakh each to return the passports.

Anirban Survivor Voice Foundation Bangladesh has asked the expatriates' welfare ministry for urgent help. It alleged that recruiting agency TK Enterprise obtained a demand for 30 workers in the name of a company in Laos, and that the workers were sent in August and September through TK Enterprise, Shining Overseas and intermediaries. It said each worker spent about Tk 6 lakh. The proprietor of Shining Overseas denied involvement. The proprietor of TK Enterprise declined to comment, the paper said.

Expatriates' Welfare Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury told The Daily Star he would look into how help could be arranged through Thailand, but announced no immediate assistance. BMET figures show 7,840 Bangladeshi workers went to Laos between January 2025 and 23 November 2026.

Why it matters

The workers left through the legal channel, with government clearance, and still ended up stranded. Migrant rights groups say this points to weak checks on job demands from new destinations. Laos has also seen raids on scam centres where Bangladeshis were among those detained.

What to watch

Whether the ministry arranges repatriation and recovers costs from the agencies, and whether BMET tightens checks on clearances for Laos.
